questions.question: Explain how one physical factor can limit the development of a country.
questions.correctAnswer: Being landlocked limits development because the country has no direct access to sea trade routes. This makes imports and exports more expensive, as goods must travel through neighbouring countries, paying transit fees and facing delays. questions.question: Describe how colonialism has contributed to uneven development.
questions.correctAnswer: Colonial powers extracted raw materials from colonies and built infrastructure only to serve export needs, not to develop local economies. They imposed artificial borders that divided ethnic groups and forced rivals together, causing conflicts that continue today. questions.question: Outline the economic causes of uneven development.
questions.correctAnswer: Economic causes include: poor trade terms (LICs export cheap primary goods and import expensive manufactured goods); debt (many LICs spend more on debt repayments than on health and education); lack of investment (poor infrastructure deters foreign investment); and exploitation by TNCs that take profits out of the country.

tests.name: Exam-Style Practice
tests.description: Short-answer practice on Uneven Development and its Consequences

questions.question: Explain why international migration is a consequence of uneven development.
questions.correctAnswer: Uneven development creates huge disparities in wealth, health, and opportunities between countries. People in LICs experience push factors (poverty, conflict, poor services) while HICs offer pull factors (jobs, safety, better services). This inequality motivates people to migrate internationally to improve their quality of life.

questions.question: Discuss the positive and negative impacts of migration on the source country.
questions.correctAnswer: Positive: Remittances provide a significant source of income (e.g. remittances make up over 30% of GDP in Tajikistan); reduced pressure on limited jobs and services; returning migrants may bring new skills and ideas. questions.correctAnswer: A balanced answer would acknowledge that physical factors (climate, landlocked position, natural hazards, lack of resources) can significantly limit development, especially in sub-Saharan Africa.
